land.text: 'upon his death in 1234, his holdings were divided between his three daughters and their husbands'; Galloway was partitioned after the revolt of 1234-1235 under the Scottish crown

correction.text: Galloway, 'south and west of the Clyde and west of the River Annan'; the historic counties of Wigtownshire and Kirkcudbrightshire, with Nithsdale, Carrick and Upper Douglasdale at times (drawn as the Dumfries and Galloway council area)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Galloway. Its Strathclyde row (644-1033) covers 13 of the 27 cells of the council area and its Kingdom of Alba row (from 1100) 14 of the 27; the rest is the Brythons row. 'The boundaries of the Kingdom of Galloway were ill-defined, and varied over time'. The council area runs east of the Annan (Eskdale) and leaves out Carrick; the two errors are about the same size and the page gives no map.

ledger.note: Page silent on a founding: 'Suibne mac Cináeda (d.1034) is the first recorded king of the Gall-ghàidhil'; the succession 'is not properly recorded until about 1138'. The Galloway page says its name comes from people who 'seem to have settled here in the 10th century', 'a people of mixed Gaelic and Norse descent', after a Brythonic kingdom was 'absorbed by the English kingdom of Bernicia' in the late 7th century. The start 1000 is a rounding of the 10th-century settlement (confidence 1).

region.text: Galloway, divided among Alan's three daughters

ledger.note: 1234: Alan of Galloway dies and the lordship is divided. 'Upon his death in 1234, his holdings were divided between his three daughters and their husbands' (Roger de Quincy, John de Balliol, William de Forz); the Galloway page adds 'a partition of Galloway, serving to fragment it administratively' after the 'Galloway revolt of 1234-1235'. The page says Galloway's 'period as an independent political entity eventually came to an end with John de Balliol delegated as Lord', undated, so 1234 is the end of the unified lordship, not of every Galwegian claim.

wars.name: Galloway revolt
wars.outcome: 'In the ensuing Galloway revolt of 1234-1235, an army of Galwegian rebels ambushed Alexander's royal army'; Gille Ruadh 'led a revolt against Alexander'; the result was 'a partition of Galloway, serving to fragment it administratively'.
wars.note: The Lordship page gives no year for Gille Ruadh's revolt; the Galloway page dates it 1234-1235.

certainty.note: The page says the boundaries 'were ill-defined, and varied over time'.

sources.title: Lordship of Galloway
sources.note: Kings and lords, Magnus III suzerainty, Fergus, 1234 division, extent, Archibald the Grim 1369.

notes: Dated items without a map effect: Magnus III 'almost certainly brought Galloway under his suzerainty' in 1098-1099 (a Norwegian overlordship, recorded from Norway's side only if at all); Fergus took the throne 'some time between 1110 and 1120', 'resigned Galloway into the hands of King Mael Coluim IV' in 1160 and died in 1161 (the Galloway page says only 'the mid-twelfth century'); in 1174 Uchtred was blinded by his brother Gille Brigte; Uchtred's son Lochlann (Roland) took the southern part and Donnchad, Gille Brigte's son, became first Earl of Carrick (undated, so no split event: Carrick has no dossier). Alan's holdings passed to Anglo-Norman husbands; in 1369 David II appointed Archibald the Grim Lord of Galloway (Galloway page: east of the Cree in 1369, west of it in 1370), a later Douglas lordship that this dossier does not cover. The page budget was two pages.
